title: Ozark Air Lines 650
summary: On December 20, 1983, while landing on Runway 3 in deteriorating visibility with snow removal operations in progress, the DC-9's right wing struck a large snowsweeping vehicle called Sweeper 7, destroying it and killing its driver Douglas Stoner. The impact ripped the right wing from the aircraft causing it to spin 180 degrees. The tower had not advised the flight crew that snow removal operations were in progress.
probable_cause: Inadequate supervision of snow removal operations by the tower; no communications had been made between the tower and the snow plow operator after the flight was handed off to the tower controller.

factors.evidence: Neither the approach nor tower controller had advised the flight that snow removal operations were in progress (p. 2)
No communications had been made between the tower and Sweeper 7 after Flight 650 was handed off to the tower controller (p. 2)
The DC-9's right wing then struck a large snowsweeping vehicle on the runway (p. 2)
The impact ripped the right wing from the plane, destroying the snow plow (p. 2)

events.text: Flight 650 departed Sioux City with weather conditions from ATIS broadcast system that included reports of blowing snow at Sioux Falls
When Flight 650 was about 4 miles out from the airport, the Sioux Falls approach controller directed the flight to contact the airport tower
The tower cleared Flight 650 to land, giving a runway visual range of 3,500 feet but did not advise of snow removal operations in progress on Runway 3
The flight crew first saw the ground and airport approach lights after descending to an altitude of 200 feet, then saw the runway
About 1,000 feet beyond the threshold of Runway 3, the aircraft made a smooth touchdown and the pilots deployed the spoilers
The DC-9's right wing then struck a large snowsweeping vehicle on the runway, ripping the right wing from the plane and destroying the snow plow with its driver, killing Douglas Stoner age 38
The plane spun through 180 degrees before coming to rest off the runway to the left of the centerline with leaking fuel briefly creating a fireball
